title: Remove contributed spam before it becomes indexable
statement: Submissions are screened for the abuse patterns the platform policy names, and material identified as abusive is withheld from public rendering rather than published and cleaned up afterwards.
rationale: A site that accepts submissions inherits responsibility for what they contain, and abusive material published even briefly is fetched, copied, and attributed to the host rather than to whoever submitted it.
implementation: Screen at submission time and hold doubtful items for a person to decide, rather than publishing immediately and relying on later reports. Retain the decision so a reversal is possible.

verification.method: Confirm a screening stage exists between submission and public rendering, and sample published contributions against the abuse categories the policy names.

caution: Whether a specific contribution is abusive is a judgement about its content, so this process reports the absence of a screening stage and never classifies individual submissions on its own authority.

sources.title: Spam policies for Google web search

title: Withhold indexing from profiles with no contributed content
statement: A member page that holds only a name and a default avatar is excluded from the index until the member has contributed something, and is admitted once they have.
rationale: Open registration generates an unbounded set of near-identical pages, and admitting them spends crawl capacity on pages that describe nothing while diluting the pages that do.
implementation: Gate the directive on a contribution count the profile renderer already knows, so a member who starts contributing becomes indexable without a separate migration.

verification.method: Request a sample of member pages spanning zero and non-zero contribution counts and compare the served indexing directive against the count each page displays.

caution: The cited documentation describes what a profile page may be marked up as, not when one should be indexed, so the threshold itself is this registry's inference and the record is tier B.

title: Keep contribution addresses resolvable after an account is removed
statement: Removing or anonymising an account leaves the contributions that remain published at their existing addresses, with attribution replaced rather than the address withdrawn, unless the contributions themselves are also being removed.
rationale: Discussions are linked to from elsewhere and quoted in replies, so deleting an account and taking its posts with it breaks conversations that other members are still part of.
implementation: Separate the account record from the contribution records so removal rewrites attribution in place. Where a contribution is genuinely withdrawn, answer its address with a removed status instead of an empty page.

verification.method: Exercise account removal against a test member with published contributions and record the status and attribution each affected address returns afterwards.

caution: Erasure obligations may require removing the contributions as well, and that determination sits with the site rather than with this process. The record governs only what happens to addresses once the scope of removal is decided.

title: Distinguish contributed material from editorial material on the page
statement: A page carrying both staff-written and member-written text marks which is which in the rendered output, so a reader can tell what the site is asserting from what someone else submitted.
rationale: Undifferentiated text reads as the site's own position, which misattributes members' claims to the publisher and hides the publisher's own claims among them.
implementation: Render contributed blocks inside a labelled region with visible attribution, and mark the same boundary in any structured description of the page so both readings agree.

verification.method: Identify pages that render both kinds of text and confirm each contributed block carries a visible label and attribution distinct from the page byline.

caution: The cited documentation provides types for describing contributed discussion but does not require visible separation, so the requirement to mark the boundary in rendered output is this registry's inference and the record is tier B.

title: Mark up a discussion only where a real discussion exists
statement: Discussion and question markup is emitted for pages that carry actual member posts or actual answers, and is absent from pages where the feature is merely available but unused.
rationale: Markup describing a conversation that has not happened misrepresents the page, and the platform documentation conditions eligibility on the content genuinely being present.
implementation: Condition emission on the rendered post count rather than on the template that could hold posts, and choose between discussion and question markup by what the page actually is rather than emitting both.

verification.method: Parse emitted discussion and question markup and confirm each declared post or answer corresponds to text the page renders.

title: Report contributed posts republished at several addresses
statement: A submission reachable through more than one address, whether by cross-posting into multiple sections or by a per-tag route, is reported so the site can decide which address is the one to index.
rationale: Every extra address for the same post competes with the others, and a site that generates them automatically multiplies its own content without adding anything a reader wants.
implementation: Enumerate the addresses each post is reachable through and compare them against the canonical value the post declares, reporting posts whose reachable set exceeds one canonical address.

verification.method: Crawl contributed sections, group responses by post identifier, and report identifiers reachable at more than one address that do not agree on a canonical value.

caution: That one post reachable at several addresses needs one nominated address is a consistency property of the site's own routing and needs no external citation. Which address to nominate depends on how the section is navigated, so the choice is reported rather than made.
